title: Elephants imitate each other when they produce deep rumbling sounds | New Scientist
description: African savannah elephants use a variety of calls to communicate, and now machine learning has shown that they tune their deepest sounds to match those of other nearby elephants
author: Christa Lesté-Lasserre

title: Placenta wrap hastens erection recovery after prostate surgery | New Scientist
description: Dried amniotic membranes from donated placentas can be wrapped around delicate nerves during prostate cancer surgery to hasten the time to a first erection after the procedure
author: Alice Klein

title: A lack of rockets is creating a crisis for space technology companies | New Scientist
description: SpaceX’s changing priorities, the war in Ukraine and a lack of competitors are all causing a launch crisis that might last years
author: Jonathan O’Callaghan

title: Anglo-Saxons got special treatment in medieval Rome | New Scientist
description: A small hoard of medieval English coins found near the Vatican in Rome suggests that early English residents held a privileged status in the holy city
author: James Woodford

title: Why a modern approach to healthcare must consider more than illness | New Scientist
description: Pills and other medications may seem like the most rigorous way to treat illness, but we increasingly know that our health must revolve around the whole mind and body
author: New Scientist

title: Slashing sugar intake before antibiotics may save your microbiome | New Scientist
description: Antibiotics can reduce the diversity of microbes in your gut and lead to health problems, but a study in people with cancer has identified a potential solution
author: Chris Simms
